existing.description_short: Trump University Founded as Fraudulent Diploma Mill

context.synopsis: Trump University was founded in 2005, charging students up to $35,000 for real estate 'seminars' that Trump promised would teach his personal investment secrets. Trump falsely claimed on promotional materials that he had 'hand-picked' instructors, when in fact instructors were chosen by a third party and given a manual instructing them to push students toward the most expensive packages using high-pressure sales tactics. The New York State Education Department informed Trump University in 2005 that it was operating illegally without a state charter, yet the school continued operating for years. Former employees described a sales-driven culture focused on extracting maximum money from vulnerable students.
context.recovered_rationale: This matters because Trump University charged vulnerable students for promised expertise, used misleading claims about instructor selection, and employed high-pressure sales tactics to steer them toward costly packages. Regulators informed the school that it lacked required authorization, yet operations continued. The record therefore documents concerns involving deceptive marketing, unlawful operation, consumer exploitation, and institutional disregard for compliance.
